To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the comorbidity of depressive and substance use disorders in adolescents is associated with the same genetic and neurobiological risk factors as the individual disorders and with additional genetic, environmental and psychological risk factors.

(1) the neurobiological systems involved in the development of depressive and substance-use disorders in adolescents and young adults include those that regulate stress responsivity, reward and motivation, and impulse control; (2) the environmental and psychosocial factors that contribute to these disorders include those that influence the development of stress, reward and impulse control systems; and (3) the comorbid conditions are likely the result of common neurobiological and environmental risk factors.

(1) the co-occurrence of substance use disorders and depressive disorders during adolescence and early adulthood is a significant public health problem; (2) the etiology of the comorbid conditions is likely to involve common genetic and environmental factors that may be mediated by neurobiological processes that include dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and the serotonergic and dopaminergic systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neurobiological and psychopathological processes that underlie the development of depressive and addictive disorders in adolescents.
understanding the mechanisms that link the development of depressive and substance related disorders in adolescents.
the identification of neurobiological and psychobiological mechanisms involved in the onset and progression of both depressive and addictive disorders in adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many similarities between depressive and substance-related disorder and that these disorders share a common neurobiological basis.
there are no definitive conclusions about the neurobiological mechanisms involved in the etiopathology of the comorbid disorder.
the mechanisms underlying the co-occurrence of depressive and addictive disorders remain to be fully elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the etiology of depression and addictive disorders are complex, involving a multitude of genetic, environmental, neurobiological and psychopathological factors.
there is a need to identify and develop new treatments for adolescents with comorbid depressive and substance-related illnesses.
the etiologies of both depressive and addictive disorders are complex and involve a variety of genetic, environmental, neurobiological and psychopathological factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neurobiological and psychobiological processes associated with depressive disorders and substance-related disorders are not mutually exclusive.
there are many commonalities between depressive and substance-related conditions, and that these commonalities are likely to be related to common neurobiological mechanisms.
the comorbidity between substance use and mood disorders in youth is not a chance association but rather is the result of common etiological factors.
